docs.title: Python Computer Visoion — Advanced Tutorials
docs.text:
A comprehensive collection of production-grade automation scripts covering file systems, web scraping, browser automation, Excel/CSV processing, email, scheduling, APIs, and more.

  1. YOLO
  2. CV2
  3. Pillow

Example — GitHub API: Auto-create Issue:

import requests

TOKEN = "your_github_token"
REPO  = "ashishbindra2/automation"

def create_issue(title, body, labels=None):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}/issues"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"token {TOKEN}"}
    data = {"title": title, "body": body, "labels": labels or []}
    r = requests.post(url, json=data, headers=headers)
    print(f"Issue created: {r.json()['html_url']}")

create_issue("Bug: Script fails on Windows", "Traceback...", ["bug"])

Example — Kill process by name:

import psutil

def kill_process(name):
    for proc in psutil.process_iter(["name", "pid"]):
        if proc.info["name"] == name:
            proc.kill()
            print(f"Killed {name} (PID {proc.info['pid']})")

kill_process("chrome.exe")

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the root:

EMAIL_USER=your@gmail.com
EMAIL_PASS=your_app_password
GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx

Load in any script with:

from dotenv import load_dotenv
import os
load_dotenv()
EMAIL_USER = os.getenv("EMAIL_USER")

docs.title: Image Processing Basics
docs.text:
• OpenCV cv2 uses BGR color format by default (cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)
  • Most deep learning models including YOLO expect RGB images.
  • When reading images using OpenCV, convert BGR → RGB before feeding into YOLO (cv2.cvcolor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))
img = cv2.imread("image.jpg")   # BGR
img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
  • Pillow (PIL) reads images in RGB format
  • CV2 was built early days so camera hardware and old library return BGR order by default

OpenCV stores and processes images in BGR format by default

Library Default Color Order OpenCV (cv2) BGR Pillow (PIL) RGB Matplotlib RGB YOLO / PyTorch / TensorFlow RGB

If you display OpenCV image directly using matplotlib:

plt.imshow(img)

colors look weird (blue ↔ red swapped).

better

plt.imshow(cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))

Why This Matters in YOLO

Wrong color order can:

  • reduce accuracy
  • hurt inference quality
  • create inconsistent training results

Most modern YOLO implementations based on the Ultralytics codebase internally handle BGR → RGB conversion when images are loaded through their official APIs.

But if you do custom preprocessing using OpenCV: then converting manually is still safest:

img = cv2.imread("image.jpg")  # BGR
img = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

docs.title: Text Clean
docs.text:
from string import whitespace
from string import punctuation

from re import sub

punctuation: str = '!"#$%&\'()*+,./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~'
table_punctuation: str = str.maketrans('','',punctuation)

def clean_txt(txt: str):
    # Remove punctuation
    no_punctuation: str = txt.translate(table_punctuation)
    # Remove digits using regex
    no_digits: str = sub(r'\d+', '', no_punctuation)
    return no_digits

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(clean_txt("ashish12323@#:$"))
